attribution: Katsushika Hokusai, public domain, via Wikimedia Commons
description: 巨浪像利爪般悬在小舟上方，富士山却安静地留在浪谷尽头。北斋用普鲁士蓝把自然的力量、人的脆弱和远景的稳定压进一张纸面的尺度中。
note: 西方的“巨浪”视觉想象，受到这件木版画及其海外传播的深刻影响。

description: Corot based his large oil painting on drawings and oil sketches made outdoors. Attracted to the beauty of the Italian countryside, he often sketched around Rome, where he lived from 1825 to 1828. This painting's highly structured composition, based on forms moving into the distance along a series of diagonals, is characteristic of Corot's early style and recalls the classical landscapes of 17th-century painter Nicholas Poussin.
note: In 1845, the French poet Charles Baudelaire proclaimed Corot the leading painter of the modern landscape.

titleZh: South Wind, Clear Sky, from Thirty-Six Views of Mount Fuji
titleEn: South Wind, Clear Sky, from Thirty-Six Views of Mount Fuji
description: Mt. Fuji, Japan’s highest mountain, appeared in most Japanese 19th-century travel literature. Maps sometimes showed its location with a Fuji-shaped icon and indicated where travelers could get the best view of it. Between 1829 and 1833, Hokusai created a print series depicting thirty-six views of the mountain, including this one, sometimes known as “Red Fuji.” The season in this scene is a time between late summer and early autumn, when the mountain takes on a reddish hue.
note: During the printing process, the natural grain of the cherry wood printing block was imprinted onto the paper along with the red-colored dye.

titleZh: The Burning of the Houses of Lords and Commons, 16 October 1834
titleEn: The Burning of the Houses of Lords and Commons, 16 October 1834
description: Fire consumed London’s famous Houses of Parliament on the night of October 16, 1834, and people gathered along the banks of the river Thames to gaze in awe at the horrifying spectacle. Initially, a low tide made it difficult to pump water to land and hampered steamers towing firefighting equipment along the river. The blaze burned uncontrollably for hours. J. M. W. Turner records the struggle as the boats in the lower-right corner head toward the flames. Although Turner based the painting on an actual event, he magnified the height of the flames, using the disaster as the starting point to express man’s helplessness when confronted with the destructive powers of nature. Brilliant swathes of color and variable atmospheric effects border on abstraction.
note: Turner painted two versions of this event. Cleveland's painting views the fire downriver, from the southeast bank of the Thames, while the second version at the Philadelphia Museum of Art views the fire from directly across Westminster Bridge.

titleZh: Tiger Hunt of Ram Singh II
titleEn: Tiger Hunt of Ram Singh II
mediumDetail: Gum tempera, ink, and gold on paper
origin: Northwestern India, Rajasthan, Rajput kingdom of Kota, court of Ram Singh II (reigned 1826–66)
description: Set against the dramatic backdrop of the cliffs that define the landscape of the small princely kingdom of Kota, a majestic tiger has just been shot by the king. Noisemakers with a firebrand drive the tiger out of the forest, and men at the right keep bears at bay. The women and musicians in two small boats look on in admiration.
note: The drummers and horn blowers proclaim to the population that the king shot a tiger.

description: Cole visited Italy in 1831 and made a small pencil sketch of this vista of Florence shortly before sunset. In his New York studio six years later, he transformed the drawing into this large oil painting, adding picturesque humans and goats to the foreground. Exhibiting View of Florence alongside a painting of the Catskill Mountains in New York in 1837, Cole set out to prove that he had mastered the very different landscapes of the Old and New Worlds.
note: Novelist Henry James grew up with this painting and described its foreground monk as his “constant friend.”

description: 巴黎繁忙大道因长时间曝光显得空旷，只有一名停留擦鞋的男子留下了身影。这通常被视为最早拍到人物的照片之一。
attribution: Louis Daguerre, Public domain, via Wikimedia Commons

titleZh: View of Schroon Mountain, Essex County, New York, After a Storm
titleEn: View of Schroon Mountain, Essex County, New York, After a Storm
description: Championing the American wilderness, Cole declared, "We are still in Eden," in his Essay on American Scenery, published two years before he painted this view of the Adirondacks. The artist sketched the scene in early summer, but when he created the painting in his studio, he rendered it in a dramatic blaze of fall colors. Such a choice likely had nationalistic overtones; he once proclaimed that autumn was "one season where the American forest surpasses all the world in gorgeousness." Cole included two Indigenous men in the painting’s right foreground foliage. At this time, the Adirondacks remained home to many Native Americans long after most had been forcibly removed from land east of the Mississippi River. While continuing to live, hunt, and fish in the area, these Algonquian and Iroquoian peoples were compelled to significantly adapt their existence amid increasing White settlement and its attendant lumber, mining, and tourist industries.
note: Nicknamed "Schroon Mountain" by the artist, the peak's official name is Hoffman Mountain.

sourceFile: Turner, J. M. W. - The Fighting Téméraire tugged to her last Berth to be broken.jpg
description: 老战舰被蒸汽拖船带向拆解场，落日把海面染成金色。透纳让一艘帆船的退场同时成为技术更替与帝国记忆的隐喻。
note: 本作曾被票选为英国最受喜爱的绘画之一。
attribution: J. M. W. Turner, Public domain, via Wikimedia Commons

titleZh: 罗伯特·科尼利厄斯自拍
description: 科尼利厄斯在费城的店铺前架好相机，自己走进画面停留片刻。这张照片被认为是美国最早的人像摄影之一，也是早期的自拍实践。
attribution: Robert Cornelius, Public domain, via Wikimedia Commons

titleZh: Winter Trees Reflected in a Pond
titleEn: Winter Trees Reflected in a Pond
mediumDetail: salted paper print from calotype negative
description: Talbot captured tree branches flawlessly mirrored on the glassy surface of the pond at his family seat, the 13th-century Lacock Abbey in Wiltshire. A longer exposure, or a lusher season, would have risked a blurred image. The result was a radically abstract composition for its time—a starkly beautiful landscape, as expressive and personal as any painting.
note: Talbot made this image just a few years after he invented the photograph on paper.

artist: 威廉·亨利·福克斯·塔尔博特
description: 塔尔博特把一盏灯、一把扫帚和半开的木门拍成安静的光影练习。日常物件在这里成为摄影从记录转向观看的早期例证。
attribution: William Henry Fox Talbot, Public domain, via Wikimedia Commons

mediumDetail: hanging scroll; ink, color, and gold on silk
description: Ukiyo-e artists’ subject matter extended to popular literature. Katsushika Ōi used color to great effect in her gruesome version of an episode from a 14th-century Chinese novel, Romance of the Three Kingdoms. Ōi portrayed the passage in which legendary 3rd-century military leader Guan Yu undergoes a bone scraping to remove poisons received from an arrow wound. In this sensationalist portrayal, Guan Yu’s attendants cower at the sight of his bloody arm while he remains unflinchingly focused on his game. As a woman, Ōi was an outlier in her era, but her talent was allowed to shine due to collaboration with her father, Katsushika Hokusai (1760–1849), the famed designer of the print known as The Great Wave .
note: This is the largest surviving painting by the artist.

description: Set in rural Long Island before the Civil War, Mount's complex painting presents an African American laborer listening intently to a fiddle tune enjoyed by white men. While a love of music unites the figures in a bond of shared humanity, the two races occupy different spaces--one inside, one outside, both separated by a barn door--effectively symbolizing the pronounced divisions in America at the time.
note: Mount was an accomplished fiddle player and even patented a new design for the instrument.

titleZh: Noah: The Eve of the Deluge
titleEn: Noah: The Eve of the Deluge
description: This painting powerfully illustrates changes in taste over time. Before it was even completed, the painting was purchased for the considerable sum of £1,000 by a newly wealthy industrialist who admired John Linnell’s modern approach to religious subjects. In 1913, however, the painting was sold at auction for only £130. Victorian painting had fallen out of favor among collectors who did not appreciate Linnell’s hotly colored landscapes that combined biblical stories and poetry (in this case Milton’s Paradise Lost ) with close study of the English landscape. Linnell was also known for financially supporting the destitute and elderly William Blake, whose mesmerizing painting of Saint Matthew is in the museum's collection.
note: Linnell was an extremely versatile artist who worked in oils and watercolors, painted miniatures on ivory, and was skilled as an engraver.

collection: 原藏德累斯顿，1945 年后失踪
description: 两名工人跪在路边敲碎石块，面孔被遮住，劳动本身成为主体。库尔贝以接近真人的尺度描绘贫困，拒绝把它美化成田园场景。
note: 原作在二战期间失踪，今天只能通过照片与复制品了解它。
attribution: Gustave Courbet, Public domain, via Wikimedia Commons

collection: 俄罗斯国家博物馆，圣彼得堡
sourceFile: Ivan Aivazovsky - The Ninth Wave - WGA00095.jpg
attribution: Ivan Aivazovsky, public domain, via Wikimedia Commons
description: 黎明将海面染成暖金色，幸存者攀住船桅，等待传说中的第九道浪。艾瓦佐夫斯基让毁灭性的海难与平静的晨光同时存在，悬念因此显得更漫长。
note: 透明色层让浪体发光，这是艾瓦佐夫斯基海景画最迷人的技术特征之一。

titleZh: Hunting Party with Badger, Loire Valley, France
titleEn: Hunting Party with Badger, Loire Valley, France
description: Hunt scenes were popular in various art forms in the mid-1800s. At that time in France, badger hunting was a working-class sport, popular among farm workers and villagers. The meat was commonly used in rural cuisine, plus badgers were considered pests. This daguerreotype shows successful hunters, dead prey at their feet, being rewarded with wine. One man, exhausted by his efforts, has dozed off. The image was definitely posed, but the dead badger suggests an element of truth behind it.
note: In the mid-1800s in France, badger hunting was a working-class sport, popular among farm workers and villagers.

mediumDetail: ten-panel screen; ink and color on silk
description: With a bird’s-eye view, this ten-panel folding screen portrays the famous Seven Jeweled Mountain 칠보산 in North Korea. Ancient volcanic eruptions shaped the mountain’s unique and awe-inspiring terrain such as phallic-shaped pillars (panel #5, from the right); a large flat-topped, steep-sided cliff (panels #7 and #8), and a rugged mountain composed of metamorphic and igneous rocks (panels #9 and #10). The tradition of landscape painting that details actual natural sites and captures their topographic features in Korea began in the 1700s and continued onward. While such natural wonders were beloved as popular destinations for tourism and pilgrimage, after the Korean War (1950–53), these sites in North Korea are no longer accessible to the outside world. This folding screen detailing the mountain’s distinctive topography feeds our imagination and longing for such an unattainable place.
note: Featuring a spectacular panoramic view and topographical details, this ten-panel folding screen is an excellent 19th-century version of the Korean “true-view” landscape painting tradition.

mediumDetail: albumen print from wet collodion negative
description: While the animals and farmers are in sharp focus in Adolphe Braun's photograph, the buildings are blurred, suggesting that perhaps Braun intended to market these photographs to visual artists as models rather than intending them to be hung on people’s walls as a substitute for a painting.
note: Oxen and horses were essential elements of 19th-century farming; they pulled the plows and other farm equipment, some of which is visible behind the animals here.

mediumDetail: salted paper print from waxed-paper negative
description: In 1851, Gustave Le Gray and his friend, photographer Auguste Mestral, traveled throughout southwestern France for the Commission of Historic French Monuments to document sites of historical importance, especially those in urgent need of, or undergoing, restoration. This image was taken from the left bank of the Tech River, situated below the old town of Palalda, four miles from the Spanish border. Le Gray stressed the rugged landscape over a close-up rendering of the ancient bridge, which was not on his list of assigned sites.
note: The sheer cliff seems to blend into the bridge mentioned in the work's title, resulting in visual uncertainty and spatial tension.

titleEn: The Great Day of His Wrath
sourceFile: John Martin - The Great Day of His Wrath - Google Art Project.jpg
description: 城市在崩塌的岩壁和火光之间被吞没，微小的人群向深渊坠落。马丁把《启示录》的末日想象变成一幅巨大的灾难全景。
note: 作品依靠戏剧性透视和发光效果，营造出近乎电影般的视觉冲击。
attribution: John Martin, Public domain, via Wikimedia Commons

mediumDetail: salted paper print from wet collodion negative
description: Édouard Baldus photographed the side of the famed cathedral to capture the volume of the structure. Visible from this angle are two workshops for the church’s restoration, some of the construction materials, and scaffolding on three of its flying buttresses (architectural structures that form an arch with the wall they support).
note: One of the major monuments of Paris, the Cathedral of Notre Dame de Paris was built in the 1100s, renovated in the 1700s, and in need of restoration by the 1800s.

collection: 大都会艺术博物馆，纽约
description: 马匹与驯马师在巴黎马市中形成不断向前推进的队列。博纳尔通过长期现场观察，准确表现动物的肌肉、动作与群体秩序。
note: 为便于写生，博纳尔曾获准穿男装进入以男性为主的马市。
attribution: Rosa Bonheur, Public domain, via Wikimedia Commons

titleEn: Valley of the Shadow of Death
sourceFile: Valley of the shadow of death.jpg
description: 荒凉山谷里散落着炮弹，没有直接出现尸体与战斗。芬顿以克制的风景式构图，记录战争留下的痕迹与死寂。
note: 作品是克里米亚战争最著名的早期战争照片之一。
attribution: Roger Fenton, Public domain, via Wikimedia Commons
